assumptions.condition: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
\(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

novel.justification: The condition permits polynomial depletion of trial enrollment at a clinically meaningful covariate boundary. Beta-type enrollment densities and smooth exponential tilts of \(x^a\) satisfy it, so it describes a concrete weak-overlap mechanism rather than an estimator-dependent rate restriction.

standard.name: target density bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).
\(c_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\le\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_p}\sup_{x\in[h/2,h]}|\mu(x)-q(x)|\le C_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\) for every dyadic \(h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The condition says that a leading boundary feature persists across resolution scales instead of disappearing through accidental polynomial cancellation. Functions of the form \(q(x)+cx^s+r(x)\), with \(c\ne0\), \(q\in\mathcal P_p\), and a smoother remainder \(r\), satisfy it, making the restriction interpretable and testable through adjacent-scale differences.

definitions.name: Polynomial-boundary transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.

definitions.name: Two-sample minimax root risk
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2},\] where the infimum ranges over all estimators measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

definitions.name: Executable cross-fitted boundary regression
definitions.construction:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.

definitions.name: Executable interior RiCOT weights and certificate role
definitions.construction:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set every calibration and target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

Both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight are measurable functions of the observed covariates. In the execution certificate the capped downstream weight enters only through the observable coefficients \(\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\). The cap still does not inherit the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations, and no held-out localization, coefficient-norm rate, leverage bound, or frontier attainment is claimed.

definitions.name: Observable RiCOT linear coefficients
Riesz-calibrated boundary-spliced estimator and linear carrier
definitions.construction:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.

After the covariates are fixed, the foldwise ridge fits are linear in the source pseudo-outcomes. With the observable coefficients defined in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\), algebraic expansion of the unchanged display gives
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i.
\]
This equality is proved in \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\); it records the estimator's certificate carrier without modifying its folds, fits, weights, or formula.

definitions.name: Observable Hölder design discrepancy
definitions.construction:
For integers \(n,m\ge2\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), define the observable Hölder design discrepancy
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=
\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\ \|v\|_\infty\le1}}
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})v(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mv(X_j^T)\right|.
\]
Equivalently, this is the maximum of the two linear optimization problems obtained by multiplying the expression inside the absolute value by \(+1\) and \(-1\), over the convex Hölder feasible set. Thus it is an exact covariate-measurable verification object. No polynomial-time evaluation claim and no stochastic-order or frontier-order claim is part of the definition.

definitions.name: Observable coefficient norm and Hoeffding radii
definitions.construction:
For integers \(n,m\ge2\), define the observable source and target Hoeffding radii
\[
R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
=\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2},
\qquad
R_T(m)=\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\gamma)}{m}}.
\]
The only source dispersion diagnostic used by the certificate is the exact observable coefficient norm \(\{\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\}^{1/2}\). No empirical variance estimator, covariance estimator, studentization, leverage condition, Gaussian approximation, or multiplier approximation is part of this construction.

definitions.name: Finite-sample RiCOT execution-certificate interval
Multiscale self-similar adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use dyadic differences of adjacent untruncated boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one interval from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}:h\text{ dyadic}\}\). The handle still does not specify the measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, selection rule, or tie breaking.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and \(h\downarrow0\), \[\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2=\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\asymp\begin{cases}1,&a<1,\\ \log(1/h),&a=1,\\ h^{1-a},&a>1.\end{cases}\] Hence the target expectation functional has a source \(L^2(P_S)\) Riesz representer if and only if \(a<1\).
statements.justification: This norm is the precise regularity threshold behind the regular, critical, and nonregular regimes.
statements.gap: The transported control-regression component in Burman et al.'s distinct target-outcome estimand uses a density-ratio representer under bounded overlap, while Khan and Tamer link large inverse weights to irregularity without computing this polynomial-boundary threshold for the present covariate-only target functional.
statements.consumer: The lemma tells analysts of the RICOT cardiomyopathy transport study whether an ordinary influence-function variance is finite before fitting a transport estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By the definitions of \(r\), \(f_S\), \(f_T\), \(g_S\), and \(g_T\), for every \(h\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2
 =\int_h^1 r(x)^2 f_S(x)\,dx
 =\int_h^1 \frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx
 =\int_h^1 x^{-a}\frac{g_T(x)^2}{g_S(x)}\,dx.
\]
The source- and target-boundary-factor assumptions give, pointwise on \([0,1]\),
\[
 \frac{c_{T,-}^2}{c_{S,+}}x^{-a}
 \le x^{-a}\frac{g_T(x)^2}{g_S(x)}
 \le \frac{c_{T,+}^2}{c_{S,-}}x^{-a}.
\]
The constants in this comparison are finite and strictly positive.  Direct integration gives
\[
 \int_h^1x^{-a}\,dx=
 \begin{cases}
 (1-h^{1-a})/(1-a),&a<1,\\
 \log(1/h),&a=1,\\
 (h^{1-a}-1)/(a-1),&a>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
This proves the displayed three-regime equivalence, uniformly over members of the class.

It remains to justify the representer assertion.  On \(L^2(P_S)\), the source component of the target-expectation functional is the linear map
\[
 L(v)=\int_0^1v(x)f_T(x)\,dx=\mathbb E_{P_S}\{r(X)v(X)\}.
\]
If \(a<1\), the preceding calculation with \(h\downarrow0\) shows that \(r\in L^2(P_S)\), so Cauchy--Schwarz makes \(L\) continuous and \(r\) is its representer.  Conversely, if \(L\) had an \(L^2(P_S)\) representer \(q\), then for every bounded measurable \(v\),
\[
 \int_0^1v(x)q(x)f_S(x)\,dx=\int_0^1v(x)f_T(x)\,dx.
\]
Because \(f_S(x)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in(0,1]\), uniqueness of Radon--Nikodym derivatives gives \(q=r\), \(P_S\)-almost surely.  For \(a\ge1\), the same integral calculation shows \(r\notin L^2(P_S)\), a contradiction.  Thus a source \(L^2(P_S)\) representer exists if and only if \(a<1\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: Suppose \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). There are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every sufficiently small \(h\), the perturbations generated by \(b_h\) yield two observed-data laws \(\mathbb P_{+,h},\mathbb P_{-,h}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) whose source marginals satisfy \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})\le Cnh^{2s+a+1},\qquad |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|\ge ch^{s+1}.\] A separate smooth target-density perturbation yields two full-data laws whose observed target projections have divergence bounded by a constant and target separation at least \(cm^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The witness converts the boundary geometry into the exact testing separation needed for the converse.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. define \(\mathcal V\) by the uniform bound \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; that construction does not cover a diverging polynomial boundary ratio, produce the exponent \((s+1)/(2s+a+1)\), or include the independent target-sample floor.
statements.consumer: The witness certifies that no alternative weighting method can improve the proposed cardiomyopathy transport rate merely by changing the optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We construct full-data extensions and verify membership in the model before computing the two separations.  Put
\[
f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,
\qquad
f_T(x)=1,
\qquad 0\le x\le1.
\tag{1}
\]
These are probability densities on the declared support.  Their nonsingular factors are \(g_S=a+1\) and \(g_T=1\).  The declared ranges \(c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\) and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\) give all density-factor bounds, while \(M\ge a+1\) gives the required radius bound.  Since both factors are constant, they belong to \(\mathcal H^t(M)\).  The two displayed restrictions involving \(s\) and \(t\) are therefore satisfied as parameter restrictions and require no additional construction.

Use the fixed known propensity \(e\), draw \(A\mid X=x\) as \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e(x))\), and make \(A\) conditionally independent of the potential outcomes given \(X\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), take Bernoulli potential outcomes with means
\[
\mu_{0,+}(x)=\mu_{0,-}(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta b_h(x).
\tag{2}
\]
Give the target potential outcomes the same conditional means.  By the scaling identity in \(\mathrm{def:boundary\text{-}bump}\), the family \(b_h(x)=h^sK(x/h)\mathbf 1\{x\le h\}\) has uniformly bounded \(\mathcal H^s\)-norm for \(0<h\le1\).  Choose the fixed number \(\delta>0\) small enough that (2) takes values in \([1/4,3/4]\), both response functions belong to \(\mathcal H^s(M)\), and
\[
\frac14-\delta^2\ge M^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
Such a choice exists because \(M>4\).  Set \(Y=Y^S(A)\).  This verifies consistency, conditional trial randomization, treatment positivity, mean transportability, response smoothness, bounded support, and residual nondegeneracy.  Thus both induced observed laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\).  Notice also that all normalizations and support conditions have been checked explicitly; no density ratio is evaluated at \(x=0\).

For \(|u|\le\delta\le1/4\), the elementary Bernoulli bound
\[
\operatorname{kl}\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12+u\right),
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12-u\right)\right)
\le \frac{4u^2}{1/4-u^2}
\le C_0u^2
\tag{4}
\]
follows from \(\operatorname{kl}(p,q)\le(p-q)^2/\{q(1-q)\}\).  The source alternatives differ only in the treated conditional outcome distribution.  Tensorization, (4), and \(e(x)\le1\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})
&\le C_0n\delta^2\int_0^h b_h(x)^2(a+1)x^a\,dx\\
&=C_0(a+1)\delta^2nh^{2s+a+1}
  \int_0^1K(u)^2u^a\,du\\
&\le Cnh^{2s+a+1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The target covariate law is common to these alternatives.  Since \(K\ge0\) is nonzero, \(k_1:=\int_0^1K(u)\,du>0\), and hence
\[
\left|\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})\right|
=2\delta\int_0^hb_h(x)\,dx
=2\delta k_1h^{s+1}.
\tag{6}
\]
This proves the source part.  The multiplier \(\delta\) may be chosen arbitrarily smaller while preserving every membership check; consequently the constant on the right of (5) may, when needed, be made arbitrarily small.

For the independent target-sample witness, retain the source density in (1), let \(\ell(x)=x-1/2\), and choose a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta_0>0\).  Keep the entire source law common, with Bernoulli potential-outcome means
\[
\mu_0(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_1(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x),
\tag{7}
\]
and put
\[
f_{T,\pm}(x)=1\pm u_m\ell(x),
\qquad
u_m=\delta_1m^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Because \(\int_0^1\ell(x)\,dx=0\), (8) gives two densities.  The strict slack \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\) permits a fixed \(\delta_1>0\) for which both densities obey the target bounds for every \(m\ge1\).  The function \(\ell\) is smooth, so reducing \(\delta_0,\delta_1\) if necessary verifies the two Hölder-radius conditions, the outcome-support condition, and (3).  Assign target potential outcomes the conditional means in (7).  This supplies admissible full-data extensions and verifies mean transportability.

Since \(f_{T,-}\) is bounded away from zero, the inequality \(\operatorname{KL}(p,q)\le\int(p-q)^2/q\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{KL}(P_{T,+}^{\otimes m},P_{T,-}^{\otimes m})
&\le m\int_0^1
 \frac{\{f_{T,+}(x)-f_{T,-}(x)\}^2}{f_{T,-}(x)}\,dx\\
&\le C_1mu_m^2\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
\le C_2\delta_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Finally, \(\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx=1/12\), so
\[
|\tau_+-\tau_-|
=2\delta_0u_m\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
=\frac{\delta_0\delta_1}{6}m^{-1/2}.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (9)--(10) establish the target part, including its full-data extension. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\), there is \(c>0\) such that \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] At \(a=1\), the source term is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\); it is obtained by a multiscale mixture of boundary bumps and has no hidden polynomial loss.
statements.justification: The converse is the theorem-level certificate that the three regimes are structural rather than artifacts of truncation.
statements.gap: Khan and Tamer establish tail-dependent irregularity. Zhang et al.'s uniformly bounded-ratio class is defined in Section 1 on page 2 and its known-law lower bound is Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; neither result derives the two-sample polynomial-boundary phase diagram or its critical logarithm.
statements.consumer: The result gives trial planners a lower bound on how much source recruitment near an underrepresented cardiomyopathy-risk boundary is needed for a desired precision.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We first record a self-contained two-point inequality.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be two observed-data laws, let \(\theta_j=\tau(Q_j)\), and put \(\Delta=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  For any estimator \(\widehat\tau\), the event \(E=\{|\widehat\tau-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\) gives
\[
\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(\widehat\tau-\theta_j)^2
\ge \frac{\Delta^2}{8}
 \{Q_0(E^c)+Q_1(E)\}
\ge \frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.
\tag{11}
\]
For completeness, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\kappa<\infty\), write \(q_0,q_1\) for densities with respect to a common dominating measure and \(A=\int\sqrt{q_0q_1}\).  Jensen's inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz give, respectively,
\[
A=\mathbb E_{Q_0}\sqrt{q_1/q_0}\ge e^{-\kappa/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
\le\sqrt{1-A^2}
\le\sqrt{1-e^{-\kappa}}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus a fixed sufficiently small Kullback--Leibler bound and a separation \(\Delta\) imply a root-mean-squared minimax lower bound \(c\Delta\).  All pairs below have common target law or common source law, so the displayed divergence is also the divergence of the complete two-sample experiment.

We next prove the source lower bound in each overlap regime without invoking any unproved source-frontier helper.  Throughout, use the admissible baseline \(f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a\), \(f_T(x)=1\), Bernoulli potential outcomes, and the full-data extension checked in \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}bump}\).

If \(a<1\), take
\[
\mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta n^{-1/2}.
\tag{13}
\]
For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), these laws are in the model for every \(n\).  The calculation in (4), now integrated against the probability density \(f_S\), gives source divergence at most \(C\delta^2\), while their target separation is \(2\delta n^{-1/2}\).  Reducing \(\delta\) and applying (11)--(12) proves
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c n^{-1/2},
\qquad a<1.
\tag{14}
\]

Suppose \(a=1\).  This is the critical multiscale step.  For all sufficiently large \(n\), set
\[
L_n=\left\lfloor\frac{\log_2 n}{4(s+1)}\right\rfloor,
\qquad x_j=2^{-j},
\qquad q_n=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{nL_n}},
\tag{15}
\]
and define the sign-aligned multiscale boundary perturbation
\[
v_n(x)=q_n\sum_{j=1}^{L_n}x_j^{-1}K(x/x_j)
=q_n\sum_{j=1}^{L_n}x_j^{-(s+1)}b_{x_j}(x).
\tag{16}
\]
Thus (16) is explicitly a multiscale mixture of the boundary bumps from \(\mathrm{def:boundary\text{-}bump}\).  Hölder scaling and a geometric sum imply
\[
\|v_n\|_{\mathcal H^s}
\le Cq_n\sum_{j=1}^{L_n}x_j^{-(s+1)}
\le Cq_nx_{L_n}^{-(s+1)}
\le C\delta\frac{n^{-1/4}}{\sqrt{L_n}},
\tag{17}
\]
because \(2^{L_n(s+1)}\le n^{1/4}\).  Hence \(\mu_{1,\pm}=1/2\pm v_n\) and \(\mu_{0,\pm}=1/2\) obey the support, Hölder, and variance conditions after a fixed reduction of \(\delta\).

It remains to compute the information and separation.  For \(x\in(x_{k+1},x_k]\), only indices \(j\le k\) can contribute and
\[
\sum_{j\le k}x_j^{-1}\le 2^{k+1}\le2x^{-1}.
\]
For \(0\le x\le x_{L_n}\), the full sum is at most \(2x_{L_n}^{-1}\).  Since \(K\le1\) and \(f_S(x)=2x\), these bounds give
\[
\int_0^1v_n(x)^2f_S(x)\,dx
\le Cq_n^2\left\{1+\int_{x_{L_n}}^1\frac{dx}{x}\right\}
\le Cq_n^2L_n.
\tag{18}
\]
The Bernoulli calculation (4) and (18) show that the \(n\)-sample source divergence is at most \(Cnq_n^2L_n=C\delta^2\).  On the other hand, nonnegativity of \(K\) and a change of variables yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_+-\tau_-|
&=2\int_0^1v_n(x)\,dx\\
&=2q_n\sum_{j=1}^{L_n}x_j^{-1}
 \int_0^{x_j}K(x/x_j)\,dx\\
&=2\delta\left(\int_0^1K(u)\,du\right)
 \sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}
\ge c\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
After reducing \(\delta\), (11)--(12) prove the critical lower bound for all sufficiently large \(n\).  For the finitely many remaining \(n\), the parametric construction (13) applies, and \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(n^{-1/2}\); decreasing the final constant covers those indices as well.  This proves the claimed logarithm without a polynomial loss.

If \(a>1\), choose
\[
h=d\,n^{-1/(2s+a+1)},
\tag{20}
\]
where \(d>0\) is fixed small enough that \(h\) lies in the range of \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}bump}\) for every \(n\ge1\).  The source pair in that lemma can be scaled so that
\[
\operatorname{KL}(Q_+,Q_-)
\le Cnh^{2s+a+1}=Cd^{2s+a+1}
\tag{21}
\]
is as small as required in (12), whereas
\[
|\tau(Q_+)-\tau(Q_-)|
\ge ch^{s+1}
=cd^{s+1}n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}.
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (11)--(12) prove the \(a>1\) branch.  Combining (14), (19), and (22) gives, for every regime,
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c_S\rho_n(a,s).
\tag{23}
\]

Finally use the target-density pair in \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}bump}\).  Its source law is common, its target-product divergence is bounded by \(C\delta_1^2\), and its parameter separation is \(c\delta_1m^{-1/2}\).  Choose the freely scalable \(\delta_1\) sufficiently small and apply (11)--(12) to obtain
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c_Tm^{-1/2}.
\tag{24}
\]
The same minimax risk appears in (23) and (24).  Therefore \(\max\{u,v\}\ge(u+v)/2\) gives
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
The critical construction (15)--(19) is the announced multiscale boundary-bump mixture. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), the unchanged spliced estimator and the observable coefficients in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\) satisfy the exact identity
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i
\]
and the exact error decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau
={}&\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\\
&+\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\mu(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)\right\}\\
&+\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau\right|
\le B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
For any realized covariate design with \(B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), the displayed certificate radius is at most
\[
b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}.
\]
This is a finite-sample execution certificate. It makes no stochastic-order, localization, leverage, minimax-attainment, or expected-length claim for \(B_X\) or the coefficient norm.
statements.justification: The result turns the unchanged RiCOT estimator into an exact, auditable finite-sample execution certificate without asserting empirical frontier attainment.
statements.gap: Published RiCOT results do not establish polynomial-boundary held-out localization for the capped continuation; the theorem therefore exposes the realized design discrepancy and coefficient norm instead of assuming or claiming their rate.
statements.consumer: A cardiomyopathy transport analysis can compute the certificate and see directly whether its realized covariate design and fitted linear coefficients support a useful finite-sample radius.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\mathcal C\) be the sigma-field generated by all source and target covariates. By the positive ridge terms in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\), each foldwise regression coefficient is a unique linear function of the source pseudo-outcomes in its training complement. The matrices and smoother coefficients in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\) are precisely the coefficients obtained from the corresponding normal equations. Therefore, for every fold \(k\) and every \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)
=\sum_{q=1}^n L_{q,k,h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)Z_q.
\tag{1}
\]
Substitution of (1) into the target plug-in term and the fitted-regression term of \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) shows that the coefficient of a fixed \(Z_q\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
{}&\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mL_{q,k_T(j),h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(q))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_q)\mathbf 1\{X_q\ge h\}\\
&\quad-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}
L_{q,k_S(i),h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Expression (2) is \(\Gamma_q(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\) by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\), proving the first identity. Every factor in (2) is \(\mathcal C\)-measurable: the ridge Gram matrices and the RiCOT primal--dual programs depend only on the observed covariates. Hence every \(\Gamma_q\) is \(\mathcal C\)-measurable.

By consistency, conditional trial randomization, and the definition of the known randomization propensity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{P_S}(Z\mid X=x)
&=\frac{\mathbb E_{P_S}(AY\mid X=x)}{e(x)}
-\frac{\mathbb E_{P_S}\{(1-A)Y\mid X=x\}}{1-e(x)}\\
&=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}\{Y^S(1)\mid X=x\}
-\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}\{Y^S(0)\mid X=x\}\\
&=\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)=\mu(x).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The divisions in (3) are valid because treatment positivity gives \(e(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). Adding and subtracting \(\sum_i\Gamma_i\mu(X_i)\) and \(m^{-1}\sum_j\mu(X_j^T)\) in the first identity gives the displayed exact error decomposition.

The H\"older norm is subadditive. Thus the two response-smoothness assumptions imply \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\). Since \(0\le\mu_d\le1\), one also has \(\|\mu\|_\infty\le1\). The definition of \(B_X\) consequently yields the pointwise, design-conditional bound
\[
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i\mu(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)\right|\le B_X.
\tag{4}
\]

Treatment positivity and \(0\le Y\le1\) imply \(-\varepsilon^{-1}\le Z_i\le\varepsilon^{-1}\). Conditional on \(\mathcal C\), the source pseudo-outcomes are independent and are centered as in (3). The conditional range length of \(\Gamma_i\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\) is at most \(2|\Gamma_i|/\varepsilon\). Applying \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\text{-}sum\text{-}hoeffding}\) conditionally with \(\delta=\gamma/2\) gives
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left(
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\right|>R_S
\,\middle|\,\mathcal C\right)\le\frac\gamma2.
\tag{5}
\]
Independence of the target sample, the identity \(\mathbb E_{P_T}\mu(X^T)=\tau\), and the bound \(\mu(X^T)\in[-1,1]\) permit a second application of the same lemma to \(m^{-1}\{\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\}\). Again using \(\delta=\gamma/2\),
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left(
\left|\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\right|>R_T(m)
\right)\le\frac\gamma2.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking expectations in (5), combining (4)--(6) with the exact decomposition, and applying the union bound prove the coverage probability. Finally, \(B_X\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\le g^2\), together with the definitions of \(R_S\) and \(R_T\), give the asserted realized-design radius. No density-smoothness condition, density-ratio localization, leverage bound, or stochastic rate for the two observable diagnostics enters the argument. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\),
\[
\frac{c_{T,-}}{c_{S,+}}\le r(x)=\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}\le\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}},\qquad 0<x\le1,
\]
\(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and
\[
h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).
\]
For every fold whose source and target interior training measures are both nonzero, the dual extension \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)\) is strictly positive for every \(x\in[h_n,1]\). These deterministic facts do not by themselves assert an empirical norm bound, a nonzero realized residual sum, or a root-risk bound.
statements.justification: The bounded-ratio arithmetic is proved, while the empirical root-risk conclusion correctly remains downstream of attainment.
statements.gap: Positivity of the extension is not a variance or risk bound.
statements.consumer: The case remains a future implementation unit test for nonzero held-out corrections and regular two-sample scaling.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(s>0\) and \(t>0\), fix a law satisfying the proposition's assumptions, and set \(a=0\). By the definitions of the density factors, for every \(x\in(0,1]\),
\[
f_S(x)=x^a g_S(x)=g_S(x),
\qquad
f_T(x)=g_T(x),
\qquad
r(x)=x^{-a}\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}=\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}.
\]
The source- and target-boundary-factor assumptions give
\[
c_{S,-}\le g_S(x)\le c_{S,+},
\qquad
c_{T,-}\le g_T(x)\le c_{T,+},
\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
Because \(c_{S,-}>0\), the denominator \(g_S(x)\) is strictly positive. Dividing the two pairs of bounds therefore yields, for every \(0<x\le1\),
\[
\frac{c_{T,-}}{c_{S,+}}
\le r(x)=\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}
\le \frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}.
\]

Since \(a=0<1\), the first branch in the definition of \(h_n\) applies and gives
\[
h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}.
\]
The condition \(s>0\) implies \(s+1>0\), so elementary exponent arithmetic gives
\[
h_n^{s+1}
=\left(n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\right)^{s+1}
=n^{-1/2}.
\]
Moreover, \(h_n\downarrow0\) as \(n\to\infty\). Applying Lemma \texttt{lem:riesz-threshold} in its \(a<1\) regime along this sequence gives
\[
\int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\asymp1.
\]
Hence the displayed integral is \(O(1)\), with finite comparison constants determined only by the fixed source and target boundary-factor constants.

It remains to prove positivity of the executable extension. Fix a fold \(k\) for which both interior training measures have positive total mass, and define
\[
I^T_{k,n}=\{j\in\mathcal T^T_k:X_j^T\ge h_n\}.
\]
Positive target interior mass implies \(I^T_{k,n}\ne\varnothing\) and \(|\mathcal T^T_k|>0\). Positive source and target interior masses exclude the zero-mass fallback in Definition \texttt{def:ricot-weights}, so either its exact-feasibility branch or its penalized branch is used. On either branch, the selected calibration and target-marginal multipliers are finite real vectors. Thus, for every \(x\in[h_n,1]\) and \(j\in I^T_{k,n}\),
\[
\exp\!\left[-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)
+\widehat\theta_{h_n,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}
\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)
+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right]>0.
\]
Indeed, the cost and spline coordinates are finite, the selected multipliers are real, and \(\eta_0>0\). Consequently the bracket in the raw continuation is a sum containing at least one strictly positive term:
\[
\frac{1}{|\mathcal T^T_k|}
\sum_{j\in I^T_{k,n}}
\exp\!\left[-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)
+\widehat\theta_{h_n,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}
\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)
+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right]>0.
\]
The outer exponent \(\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)\) is strictly positive because \(\eta_0,\lambda_0>0\). Therefore
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)>0,
\qquad x\in[h_n,1].
\]
When \(a=0\), the deterministic downstream cap is
\[
\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h_n^{-a}=\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}>0.
\]
The capped RiCOT extension is the minimum of this positive cap and the positive raw continuation. Thus, for every \(x\in[h_n,1]\),
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)
=\min\!\left\{
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x),
\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}
\right\}>0.
\]

Every conclusion is deterministic conditional on the positive-interior-mass branch. The argument uses the density-factor bounds, the bandwidth definition, the Riesz threshold, and the RiCOT construction, but no additional smoothness inequality involving \(s\) or \(t\). It therefore holds for all declared \(s>0\) and \(t>0\), in particular under the two smoothness inequalities stated in the proposition. Positivity alone supplies no empirical norm bound, no nonzero realized residual sum, and no root-risk conclusion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(M\ge a+1\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), there is \(c>0\) such that
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\left\{m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}
n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\
\sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\
n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.
\end{cases}\right\}.
\]
This lower phase diagram requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds. Moreover, uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Thus the proved minimax lower frontier matches the exact truncated-oracle envelope; no data-driven minimax upper bound is asserted.
statements.justification: The corrected node states the maximal proved lower frontier and its matching truncated-oracle benchmark.
statements.gap: A measurable data-driven minimax upper witness remains unavailable because empirical RiCOT stability is unresolved.
statements.consumer: The result provides a precision impossibility and oracle-benchmark phase diagram for transported effects.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By \(\mathrm{lem:source\text{-}only\text{-}frontier\text{-}lower}\), there is a constant \(c_0>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(m\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c_0\rho_n(a,s).
\tag{1}
\]
The subexperiments proving that lemma have \(f_T=1\).  The declared parameter ranges give \(c_{T,-}\le 1\le c_{T,+}\), so those subexperiments remain admissible when either target-density bound is attained.  Thus (1) requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds.

By \(\mathrm{ass:sample\text{-}balance}\), \(m/n\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\).  Consequently, there are constants \(c_\kappa,C_\kappa>0\) and an integer \(n_0\) such that
\[
 c_\kappa n\le m\le C_\kappa n
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(n\ge n_0\).  In particular,
\[
 m^{-1/2}\le c_\kappa^{-1/2}n^{-1/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
In every overlap regime, \(n^{-1/2}\) is bounded above by a fixed multiple of \(\rho_n(a,s)\).  Indeed,
\[
 \rho_n(a,s)=n^{-1/2}\qquad\text{if }a<1,
\tag{4}
\]
while, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_n(1,s)=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\ge n^{-1/2}.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(a>1\), then
\[
 \frac{s+1}{2s+a+1}<\frac12,
\]
and hence
\[
 \rho_n(a,s)=n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\ge n^{-1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (3)--(6) imply that, eventually,
\[
 m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\le C_1\rho_n(a,s)
\tag{7}
\]
for a finite constant \(C_1\) depending only on the fixed parameters and \(\kappa\).  Combining (1) and (7) gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
 \ge \frac{c_0}{C_1}\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Substitution of the three branches in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\) proves the displayed lower phase diagram.

The already established \(\mathrm{lem:oracle\text{-}truncation\text{-}envelope}\) gives, uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
 m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}
 +n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
 \asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\tag{9}
\]
This is an order identity for a deterministic boundary-approximation term and the exact truncated source representer.  It does not construct an estimator measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), so (9) is not a minimax upper bound.  Equations (8)--(9) prove exactly the lower phase diagram and its truncated-oracle benchmark. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). The interval \(\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\) satisfies the finite-sample fixed-class coverage guarantee
\[
\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}
\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Its realized length is exactly
\[
2\{B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\}.
\]
In particular, on any realized covariate design for which \(B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), its length is at most
\[
2\left\{b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}\right\}.
\]
No expected-length rate, Gaussian approximation, multiplier approximation, variance consistency, leverage control, or empirical frontier attainment is asserted.
statements.justification: The corrected interval gives uniform finite-sample fixed-class coverage from bounded outcomes, with every contribution to its realized radius observable.
statements.gap: The previous folded-normal construction required unproved Gaussian, multiplier, and variance approximations; the replacement proves coverage without any of those approximations and makes no expected-length-rate claim.
statements.consumer: The RICOT cardiomyopathy application can report this interval as a realized-design certificate while separately disclosing that a frontier-order length guarantee is not established.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), the event \(\tau\in\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) is exactly
\[
\left|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau\right|
\le B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m).
\tag{1}
\]
For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\) assigns probability at least \(1-\gamma\) to (1). The bound is uniform in the law, so taking the infimum over the same model class proves the fixed-class coverage display.

The interval is symmetric about \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) with half-length \(B_X+R_S+R_T\); hence its realized length is exactly twice that sum. On a design satisfying \(B_X\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\le g^2\), the definitions of the radii give
\[
R_S\le\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g,
\qquad
R_T(m)=\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}.
\]
Substitution proves the final length bound. These are deterministic statements about the realized design and do not entail an expected-length rate or empirical frontier attainment. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Fix \(a>1\), \(t>1/2\), and \(0<s_1<s_2\) such that \(s_\ell/(2s_\ell+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for \(\ell\in\{1,2\}\), and suppose \(M\ge a+1\) and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). Any confidence interval with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\cup\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\) has, at some law in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\), expected length at least \(c\{m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}\}\).
statements.justification: The theorem prevents data-driven smoothness selection from being advertised as honest without an explicit restriction that makes boundary bias observable.
statements.gap: Cai and Low characterize adaptation by between-class moduli, but the ordered modulus for a transported functional under source density \(x^a\), including the transition through \(a=1\), has not been computed.
statements.consumer: The result tells clinical transport analysts when prespecifying a smoothness class is unavoidable for valid interval length claims.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We first derive the interval inequality used below.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) have parameter values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be any random interval.  If
\[
Q_0\{\theta_0\in\mathcal C\}\ge1-\gamma-r,
\qquad
Q_1\{\theta_1\in\mathcal C\}\ge1-\gamma-r,
\tag{25}
\]
then transfer of the second event from \(Q_1\) to \(Q_0\) and the union bound show
\[
Q_0\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in\mathcal C\}
\ge1-2\gamma-2r-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1).
\tag{26}
\]
On this event the interval length is at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}|\mathcal C|
\ge |\theta_1-\theta_0|
 \{1-2\gamma-2r-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.
\tag{27}
\]
The affinity calculation (12) shows directly that a Kullback--Leibler bound tending to zero, or a sufficiently small fixed bound, makes the total variation in (27) smaller than any prescribed number in \((0,1)\).

We now construct all alternatives around one smoother reference law.  Put
\[
f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,
\qquad
f_T(x)=1,
\qquad
\ell(x)=x-\frac12.
\tag{28}
\]
Choose a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta_0>0\), and take Bernoulli potential outcomes with
\[
\mu_0(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_1(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x).
\tag{29}
\]
Use the fixed known propensity, conditional randomization, consistency, and target potential outcomes with the same conditional means.  The factor functions \(g_S=a+1\) and \(g_T=1\) satisfy the support, normalization, positivity, overlap, and order-\(t\) Hölder conditions.  Because \(\ell\) is smooth, reducing \(\delta_0\) puts (29) strictly inside both the order-\(s_1\) and order-\(s_2\) radius-\(M\) response balls and preserves the residual-variance lower bound.  Denote the induced two-sample law by \(Q_0\).  In particular,
\[
Q_0\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q_0\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t).
\tag{30}
\]

For the rough alternative, set
\[
h=d\,n^{-1/(2s_1+a+1)},
\qquad
b_{h,s_1}(x)=h^{s_1}K(x/h)\mathbf 1\{0\le x\le h\},
\tag{31}
\]
where \(d>0\) will be chosen small, and replace only the treated response by
\[
\mu_{1,1}(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x)+\delta b_{h,s_1}(x).
\tag{32}
\]
Hölder scaling and a sufficiently small fixed \(\delta>0\) put the resulting law \(Q_1\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\); all other member properties remain those checked in (28)--(30).  The Bernoulli probabilities in (29) are uniformly separated from zero and one, so the calculation in (5), with \(s=s_1\), yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
\le Cn\delta^2h^{2s_1+a+1}
=C\delta^2d^{2s_1+a+1},
\tag{33}
\]
while
\[
\Delta_S:=|\tau(Q_1)-\tau(Q_0)|
=\delta h^{s_1+1}\int_0^1K(u)\,du
\ge c_Sn^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}.
\tag{34}
\]
Choose \(d\) and \(\delta\) so that the total variation implied by (12) is some \(\eta_S<1-2\gamma\).

Let \(\mathcal C_{n,m}\) have the asserted uniform asymptotic coverage.  Along the indexing sequence in that assertion, uniformity supplies a deterministic \(r_{n,m}\to0\) for which (25) holds with \(Q_0,Q_1\) and \(r=r_{n,m}\).  Equations (27), (33), and (34) then give, at the smoother law \(Q_0\),
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}|\mathcal C_{n,m}|
\ge c_1n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}
\tag{35}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.

For the target-sample alternative, keep the source law and response functions in (28)--(29) unchanged and replace only the target density by
\[
f_{T,2}(x)=1+u_m\ell(x),
\qquad
u_m=\delta_1m^{-1/2}.
\tag{36}
\]
The strict target-density slack, smoothness of \(\ell\), and a sufficiently small fixed \(\delta_1>0\) make the resulting law \(Q_2\) a member of both response-smoothness classes.  The target calculation in (9), now comparing (36) with the uniform density, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(Q_2,Q_0)\le C\delta_1^2,
\qquad
\Delta_T:=|\tau(Q_2)-\tau(Q_0)|
=\delta_0u_m\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
=\frac{\delta_0\delta_1}{12}m^{-1/2}.
\tag{37}
\]
Reduce \(\delta_1\) so that the associated total variation is \(\eta_T<1-2\gamma\).  Uniform coverage and (27), again under the identical smoother reference law \(Q_0\), imply
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}|\mathcal C_{n,m}|\ge c_2m^{-1/2}.
\tag{38}
\]
Both (35) and (38) hold at the same law \(Q_0\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\).  Using \(\max\{u,v\}\ge(u+v)/2\) proves
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}|\mathcal C_{n,m}|
\ge c\left\{m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}\right\}.
\]
This is the asserted nonadaptation bound.  Every perturbation remains on the common support \([0,1]\), every density is normalized and positive, and no additional balance condition on \(m/n\) is used. \(\square\)

statements.statement: The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.
statements.justification: This negative answer isolates the formal obstruction before any adaptive coverage claim is attempted.
statements.gap: The frozen multiscale handle is descriptive rather than an executable selection rule, so existing self-similarity theory cannot yet be applied to it.
statements.consumer: A downstream construction must specify the measurable diagnostics, thresholds, selection map, and tie breaking before it can be used in the RICOT cardiomyopathy analysis.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
\mathsf D_{n,m}
=\bigl(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1]\bigr)^n\times\mathcal X^m
\]
carry its product Borel \(\sigma\)-field. An interval-valued statistic must, at a minimum, be a single-valued measurable map
\[
T_{n,m}:\mathsf D_{n,m}\longrightarrow
\bigl\{[\ell,u]:\ell,u\in\mathbb R,\ \ell\le u\bigr\}.
\]
Equivalently, it must specify measurable endpoint functions \(L_{n,m}\) and \(U_{n,m}\) satisfying
\[
T_{n,m}(d)=[L_{n,m}(d),U_{n,m}(d)]
\quad\text{and}\quad
L_{n,m}(d)\le U_{n,m}(d)
\]
for every realized data array \(d\in\mathsf D_{n,m}\).

By \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\), the candidate family is
\[
\left\{\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}:
h\text{ is an admissible dyadic boundary bandwidth}\right\}.
\]
The construction instructs the user to form adjacent-scale boundary local-polynomial differences, to estimate \(a\) from empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and to combine these quantities with interior Riesz-calibration residuals. It gives no formula for a measurable estimator of \(a\) or of the boundary regularity, no numerical threshold for an adjacent-scale comparison, no rule mapping the resulting diagnostics to one admissible dyadic \(h\), and no convention for choosing among multiple admissible candidates.

Consequently, the construction specifies neither endpoint functions \(L_{n,m},U_{n,m}\) nor an equivalent measurable bandwidth selector
\[
\widehat h_{n,m}:\mathsf D_{n,m}\longrightarrow
\{h:h\text{ is an admissible dyadic boundary bandwidth}\}
\]
such that
\[
T_{n,m}(d)
=\mathcal I_{\widehat h_{n,m}(d),J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}(d).
\]
Equivalently, it does not specify a measurable selected triple
\[
\bigl(\widehat h_{n,m},J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}\bigr).
\]

This is a definitional obstruction, not a stochastic remainder. Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:boundary\text{-}self\text{-}similarity}\) restricts a member law; it does not itself select a bandwidth for a realized data array. The written handle is compatible with distinct completions that choose different dyadic bandwidths whenever several candidates satisfy an unspecified comparison, and the handle selects none of those completions. Hence it does not define a single interval-valued statistic.

Because the handle defines no random interval \(T_{n,m}\), neither
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\tau\in T_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})\right\}
\]
nor
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}\!\left[
U_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})-L_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})
\right]
\]
is an evaluable quantity attached to \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\). The frozen handle therefore yields neither an adaptive coverage guarantee nor an adaptive expected-length guarantee. A positive result first requires explicit measurable diagnostics, numerical thresholds, a single-valued dyadic-bandwidth selection rule, and deterministic tie breaking. This proves the theorem. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For the deterministic regime bandwidth \(h_n\), the truncated oracle representer obeys \[m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).\] Thus the exact boundary-bias and oracle source-standard-deviation balance has the regular, critical, and nonregular rates in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By \(\mathrm{lem:riesz\text{-}threshold}\), uniformly over the model class,
\[
 \left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
 \asymp
 \begin{cases}
 1,&a<1,\\
 \sqrt{\log(1/h)},&a=1,\\
 h^{(1-a)/2},&a>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
If \(a<1\), then \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), so \(h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2}\), and the oracle stochastic term is also of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  If \(a=1\), then
\[
 h_n^{s+1}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}},
 \qquad
 \log(1/h_n)=\frac{\log n-\log\log n}{2(s+1)}\asymp\log n,
\]
and hence \(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log(1/h_n)}\asymp\sqrt{\log n/n}\).  If \(a>1\), writing \(D=2s+a+1\) gives
\[
 h_n^{s+1}=n^{-(s+1)/D},
\]
and
\[
 n^{-1/2}h_n^{(1-a)/2}
 =n^{-1/2+(a-1)/(2D)}
 =n^{-(s+1)/D}.
\]
The three cases are exactly \(\rho_n(a,s)\); adding the independent term \(m^{-1/2}\) proves the claim. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For fixed spline degree and equally spaced knots on \([h,1]\), the normalized local B-spline basis has uniformly bounded overlap and a partition of unity; its Lebesgue Gram matrix has eigenvalues comparable to \(J^{-1}\); and every radius-one Hölder function of order \(u\) has a spline approximant with uniform error at most \(C J^{-u}\), where \(C\) depends only on \(u\) and the degree.

attestation.note: Stable publisher handle supplied for the fixed-degree local B-spline stability and Hölder approximation facts used here.

statements.statement:
If \(A_1,\ldots,A_N\) are independent centered self-adjoint matrices of dimension \(d\), \(\|A_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L\) almost surely, and \(\|\sum_i\mathbb E(A_i^2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le v\), then for every \(x>0\),
\[
\mathbb P\left\{\left\|\sum_{i=1}^NA_i\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge x\right\}
\le2d\exp\left\{-\frac{x^2/2}{v+Lx/3}\right\}.
\]

attestation.note: Stable arXiv handle supplied for the bounded self-adjoint matrix Bernstein inequality.

statements.statement:
There is a universal constant \(C\) such that, for independent centered real variables \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\) with \(0<\sigma^2=\sum_i\mathbb E(W_i^2)<\infty\) and \(\sum_i\mathbb E|W_i|^3<\infty\),
\[
\sup_z\left|\mathbb P\left\{\sigma^{-1}\sum_iW_i\le z\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|
\le C\sigma^{-3}\sum_i\mathbb E|W_i|^3.
\]

statements.statement:
Let \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\) be independent real random variables with \(\mathbb E W_i=0\) and \(W_i\in[\alpha_i,\beta_i]\) almost surely. For every \(\delta\in(0,1)\),
\[
\mathbb P\!\left\{\left|\sum_{i=1}^N W_i\right|>
\sqrt{\frac12\log(2/\delta)\sum_{i=1}^N(\beta_i-\alpha_i)^2}\right\}\le\delta.
\]
The same statement holds conditionally on a sigma-field when conditional independence, conditional centering, and the displayed conditional bounds hold almost surely.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
First consider a centered random variable \(W\in[\alpha,\beta]\) and put \(d=\beta-\alpha\). Convexity of the exponential gives
\[
e^{\lambda W}\le\frac{\beta-W}{d}e^{\lambda\alpha}+\frac{W-\alpha}{d}e^{\lambda\beta}.
\]
Taking expectations and using \(\mathbb EW=0\), the logarithm of the right-hand side is the cumulant generating function of a two-point variable with range \(\lambda d\), mean zero, value zero and first derivative zero at \(\lambda=0\). Its second derivative is a Bernoulli variance and is at most \(d^2/4\). Twice integrating this second-derivative bound yields
\[
\mathbb E e^{\lambda W}\le e^{\lambda^2d^2/8}.
\tag{1}
\]
For independent \(W_i\), (1) and multiplication of moment generating functions give, with \(D=\sum_i(\beta_i-\alpha_i)^2\),
\[
\mathbb P\!\left\{\sum_iW_i\ge x\right\}
\le\inf_{\lambda>0}\exp\{-\lambda x+\lambda^2D/8\}
=\exp\{-2x^2/D\}.
\]
Applying the same argument to \(-W_i\) and adding the two tail probabilities gives \(2e^{-2x^2/D}\). Substitution of \(x^2=D\log(2/\delta)/2\) proves the assertion. The conditional version repeats the same moment-generating-function calculation with conditional expectations; all inequalities hold almost surely before the final expectation is taken. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), and \(M\ge a+1\), there is \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every \(m\),
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\rho_n(a,s).
\]
No strict inequality in the target-density bounds is required. At \(a=1\), the source lower bound is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and is generated by a multiscale sign mixture whose target covariate law is common to all mixture components.
statements.justification: This source-only converse removes an unnecessary target-density-slack restriction from the lower phase diagram.
statements.gap: A one-bump argument gives the nonregular branch but not the critical logarithm; the proof supplies the required multiscale mixture.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the no-slack lower-bound input for the repaired frontier theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We construct explicit subexperiments contained in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\).  Their source and target density factors are constant, so the construction satisfies every declared density smoothness condition for every \(t>0\); in particular, the two displayed restrictions involving \(s\) and \(t\) are not needed by the testing calculation itself.

We first record the elementary testing inequality used in all three regimes.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be two observed-data laws with parameter values \(\tau_0,\tau_1\), and put \(d=|\tau_1-\tau_0|\).  Given any estimator \(\widehat\tau\), define a test by choosing the nearer of \(\tau_0\) and \(\tau_1\).  A testing error under \(Q_u\) implies \(|\widehat\tau-\tau_u|\ge d/2\).  Since the sum of the two testing errors is at least \(1-\|Q_0-Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
 \max_{u\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_u}
       [ (\widehat\tau-\tau_u)^2]
 \ge \frac{d^2}{8}
       \{1-\|Q_0-Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For completeness, data processing of relative entropy by the indicator of a measurable set, followed by the binary calculation below, gives Pinsker's inequality.  If the set has probabilities \(p\) and \(q\), then
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}.
\]
For fixed \(q\), subtracting \(2(p-q)^2\) from the right-hand side yields a function which vanishes with zero first derivative at \(p=q\) and has second derivative
\[
 \frac1{p(1-p)}-4\ge0.
\]
Taking the supremum over measurable sets therefore gives
\[
 \|Q_0-Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2
 \le \frac12\operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus a pair with sufficiently small constant Kullback--Leibler divergence has root mean-squared risk bounded below by a constant multiple of its parameter separation.

For every regime, take
\[
 f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,
 \qquad f_T(x)=1,
 \qquad 0\le x\le1.
\tag{3}
\]
These functions integrate to one, and their nonsingular factors are \(g_S=a+1\) and \(g_T=1\).  The parameter ranges imply
\[
 c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+},
 \qquad c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}.
\tag{4}
\]
Both factors are constant and hence belong to \(\mathcal H^t(M)\), because \(M\ge a+1\).  In particular, (3)--(4) use no strict inequality in either target-density bound.

Draw \(A\) according to the fixed known propensity \(e(X)\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), let the two source potential outcomes be independent Bernoulli variables with the arm-specific means specified below, independently of \(A\); give the target potential outcomes the same conditional means.  Finally set \(Y=Y^S(A)\).  These choices satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:trial\text{-}randomization}\), \(\mathrm{ass:known\text{-}propensity}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}transportability}\).  Because \(M>4\),
\[
 \Delta_M:=\sqrt{\frac14-\frac1M}>0.
\]
All perturbation constants below are chosen small enough that each conditional mean differs from \(1/2\) by at most \(\Delta_M/2\).  The outcomes then lie in \([0,1]\), and, for either treatment arm,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)
 \ge \frac14-\frac{\Delta_M^2}{4}
 >\frac1M.
\tag{5}
\]
The control regression is constant, and the scaling arguments below place every treated regression in \(\mathcal H^s(M)\).  Thus all remaining member conditions hold.  The target covariate law in (3) is common to all alternatives, so the \(m\) target observations contribute zero divergence for every \(m\).

\emph{The nonregular case \(a>1\).}
For \(h\in(0,1)\) and a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), let
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta b_h(x).
\tag{6}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:boundary\text{-}bump}\), dilation multiplies a derivative of order \(v\le\lfloor s\rfloor\) by \(h^{s-v}\) and preserves the order-\(s\) H\"older seminorm up to the fixed norm of \(K\).  Reducing \(\delta\) if necessary therefore puts both regressions in \(\mathcal H^s(M)\), uniformly in \(h\).

For \(|u|\) in a fixed neighborhood of zero, direct calculation and Taylor's theorem give
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\!\left(
  \operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12+u\right),
  \operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12-u\right)
 \right)
 =2u\log\frac{1+2u}{1-2u}
 \le C_0u^2.
\tag{7}
\]
The control-arm conditional laws agree, while the treated-arm contribution is multiplied by \(e(x)\le1\).  Additivity of relative entropy for product laws, (3), and (7) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,\otimes n},P_{-,h}^{S,\otimes n})
 &\le Cn\int_0^h b_h(x)^2x^a\,dx\\
 &=Cnh^{2s+a+1}\int_0^1K(u)^2u^a\,du.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Because \(K\) is nonnegative and nonzero,
\[
 k_1:=\int_0^1K(u)\,du>0,
 \qquad
 |\tau_+-\tau_-|=2\delta k_1h^{s+1}.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose \(h=c_0n^{-1/(2s+a+1)}\), where \(c_0>0\) is small enough that (8) is bounded by a sufficiently small constant.  Equations (1)--(2) and (9) imply
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
 \ge c n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}.
\tag{10}
\]

\emph{The regular case \(a<1\).}
Choose a nonnegative, nonzero \(C^\infty\) function \(q\) supported in \([1/4,3/4]\), and set
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta n^{-1/2}q(x).
\tag{11}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), (11) satisfies the same range, variance, and H\"older conditions.  On the support of \(q\), the source density is bounded above and below by positive constants.  Therefore (7) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+^{S,\otimes n},P_-^{S,\otimes n})
 \le C\delta^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Under the uniform target density,
\[
 |\tau_+-\tau_-|
 =2\delta n^{-1/2}\int_0^1q(x)\,dx
 \ge c n^{-1/2}.
\tag{13}
\]
After reducing \(\delta\), equations (1)--(2), (12), and (13) prove
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c n^{-1/2}.
\tag{14}
\]

\emph{The critical case \(a=1\).}
Put \(\ell_j=2^{-j}\), fix an integer \(j_0\ge1\), and choose \(L=L_n\) so that
\[
 \ell_L\asymp n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}},
 \qquad
 L-j_0+1\asymp\log n.
\tag{15}
\]
For \(j_0\le j\le L\), define
\[
 \phi_j(x)=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt n\,\ell_j}
 K\!\left(\frac{x-\ell_j}{\ell_j}\right)
 \mathbf 1\{\ell_j\le x\le2\ell_j\}.
\tag{16}
\]
For \(\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{L-j_0+1}\), let
\[
 \mu_{0,\omega}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\omega}(x)=\frac12+
 \sum_{j=j_0}^L\omega_j\phi_j(x).
\tag{17}
\]
The shell interiors are disjoint.  Moreover, (15) implies
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n\,\ell_j}
 \le C\ell_j^s,
 \qquad j_0\le j\le L.
\tag{18}
\]
The conventional smooth-bump extension of \(K\) is flat at the endpoints of its support.  Hence each shell piece in (16), extended by zero, has order-\(s\) H\"older norm at most \(C\delta\) by (18).  The dyadic shell separation and endpoint flatness bound the cross-shell H\"older quotients by the same constant.  Thus the sum in (17) has H\"older norm at most \(C'\delta\), independently of \(L\).  Choosing \(\delta\) sufficiently small makes every sign alternative a member of the model and enforces (5).

The contribution of coordinate \(j\) to the target parameter is
\[
 d_j:=\int_{\ell_j}^{2\ell_j}\phi_j(x)\,dx
 =\frac{\delta k_1}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{19}
\]
If \(\omega^{(j)}\) is obtained by flipping only coordinate \(j\), then \(f_S(x)=2x\), and (7) implies
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_\omega^{S,\otimes n},
                    P_{\omega^{(j)}}^{S,\otimes n})
 \le Cn\int_{\ell_j}^{2\ell_j}\phi_j(x)^2x\,dx
 \le C\delta^2,
\tag{20}
\]
uniformly in \(j\), \(n\), and the other signs.

Place the uniform product prior \(\Pi\) on \(\omega\).  The covariate likelihood is sign-free, and every observed outcome involves at most one shell coordinate.  The likelihood, prior, and therefore the posterior factor across coordinates.  Since conditional expectation minimizes squared loss and \(\tau_\omega=\sum_{j=j_0}^Ld_j\omega_j\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\tau}
 \mathbb E_\Pi[(\widehat\tau-\tau_\omega)^2]
 =
 \mathbb E_\Pi\operatorname{Var}
       (\tau_\omega\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})
 =\sum_{j=j_0}^Ld_j^2
   \mathbb E_\Pi\operatorname{Var}
       (\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m}).
\tag{21}
\]
Write \(q_j=\mathbb E_\Pi(\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})\).  Then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})
 =1-q_j^2\ge1-|q_j|.
\tag{22}
\]
Let \(\overline P_{j,+}\) and \(\overline P_{j,-}\) be the mixture experiments conditional on \(\omega_j=1\) and \(\omega_j=-1\), respectively.  Bayes' formula gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\Pi|q_j|
 =\|\overline P_{j,+}-\overline P_{j,-}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{23}
\]
Pair every sign vector with its \(j\)-flip.  Convexity of relative entropy, equivalently the pointwise log-sum inequality applied to the paired mixture densities, and (20) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\overline P_{j,+},\overline P_{j,-})
 \le 2^{-(L-j_0)}
 \sum_{\omega:\,\omega_j=1}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_\omega,P_{\omega^{(j)}})
 \le C\delta^2.
\tag{24}
\]
The target factors cancel in (24) because their law is common.  Equations (2), (22)--(24), and a sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_\Pi\operatorname{Var}
   (\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})
 \ge c_1>0
\tag{25}
\]
uniformly in \(j\).  Since the supremum risk dominates the Bayes risk, (15), (19), (21), and (25) give
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_\omega[(\widehat\tau-\tau_\omega)^2]
 \ge c_1\sum_{j=j_0}^Ld_j^2
 \ge c\frac{\log n}{n}.
\tag{26}
\]
Taking square roots proves the critical lower bound \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\) without a hidden polynomial loss.

The three bounds (10), (14), and (26), together with \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\), prove that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every \(m\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Every subexperiment used the boundary-attaining target density \(f_T=1\), so no strict target-density slack is required. \(\square\)

sampling_model.design: At each triangular-array index \((n,m)\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), induced by full-data laws \(F^S_{n,m}\) and \(F^T_{n,m}\) through the projections \(\pi_S\) and \(\pi_T\). The condition \(m/n\to\kappa\) applies only to theorem sequences.
sampling_model.units: Source full-data units are \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\) and are observed as \(O^S=\pi_S(W^S)=(X,A,Y)\); target full-data units are \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\) and are observed only as \(X^T=\pi_T(W^T)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary source treatment has known probability \(e(X)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The source density is \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\), where \(c_{S,-}\le g_S\le c_{S,+}\) and \(0<c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\); the target density is \(f_T(x)=g_T(x)\), where \(c_{T,-}\le g_T\le c_{T,+}\) and \(0<c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Under the separate primitive conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, deterministic five-fold regression uses ridge-regularized order-\(p\) boundary local polynomials and degree-\(q\) interior B-splines. Interior weights solve the squared-distance semi-unbalanced entropic program with schedules \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), equally spaced knots, and \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\); normalized dual potentials give a measurable exponential extension evaluated on held-out source covariates. Inference uses the displayed fold-centered source and target multiplier process and the displayed target, interior-source, boundary-source, and source-covariance variance terms.

estimand_functional: \(\tau=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\), targeted by the unchanged \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) using the capped downstream RiCOT weight. Conditional on the covariates, the estimator has the exact observable expansion \(\sum_i\Gamma_i Z_i\), which yields a finite-sample Hoeffding execution certificate with realized radius \(B_X+R_S+R_T\). The proved rate result is the one-sided minimax lower phase diagram with its matching truncated-oracle envelope; held-out capped-weight localization, empirical frontier attainment, and a frontier-order expected-length guarantee remain open.

tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even when the real-world target population retains positive mass there. In the full-data triangular-array model, the causal target is identified as the observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The source contribution to root mean-squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\) below the square-integrability threshold \(a=1\), becomes \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at the threshold, and is \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) above it, in addition to the independent target-sample term \(m^{-1/2}\). Under the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, a fully specified squared-distance Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced transport program is truncated to the overlap interior and spliced to a deterministic boundary local polynomial. Matching bump and multiscale lower bounds, a fully evaluable fixed-Hölder-class interval with a \(2M\) bias envelope and explicit foldwise multiplier and covariance terms, and a nonadaptation theorem complete the fixed-class program; honest joint adaptation is posed only on an explicit boundary self-similar subclass.

project_justification.gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
project_justification.niche: Polynomial trial depletion with a positive target boundary density creates an estimable causal mean whose information geometry changes exactly at \(a=1\); the target sample also imposes a separate parametric floor.
project_justification.fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.

related_work: Burman et al. (2026) are the optimization and application anchor, not a nested estimand comparator. Their target unit contains an observed outcome. Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; this core instead observes only target covariates and targets \(\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)]\). Their Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 imposes bounded target-to-trial density ratio, Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14 proves calibrated-weight consistency, Theorem 5.2 on page 16 gives efficient inference for their estimand, and Section 8 on pages 23--24 studies 30-month mortality in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Section S4.3 is the source locator for the standard one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve threshold \(t>1/2\).
